column6: The upstream row carries こちら's gloss verbatim — item こちら is "this person (polite); this way (polite)". あちら is the あ-series distal demonstrative (far from BOTH speaker and listener), the polite counterpart of あそこ/あっち. As shipped the card taught the opposite of what the word means. https://jisho.org/search/あちら
Correct in sense, but indistinguishable from あちら on a card once あちら is fixed. The register IS the difference between them, so it belongs in the first clause.

そ-series, not あ-series. Jisho: "that way; that direction — direction distant from the speaker, CLOSE TO THE LISTENER". "over there" is the あ-series meaning, and the bank gave あちら, あっち, そちら and そっち the same gloss, erasing the whole こそあど distance grid. No comma before "near you": shortMeaning() would cut it off. https://jisho.org/search/そちら
Same defect as そちら, casual register. Jisho gives the identical distance note. https://jisho.org/search/そっち

column5: to become empty (vacant), to become free
column6: The senses are in the wrong order and shortMeaning() takes the first clause, so the card showed "to open" — which is 開く【あく】's meaning, for its homophone whose whole point is that it is NOT 開く. Jisho's first sense is "to become less crowded; to thin out; to get empty"; "to open" is only sense 3. https://jisho.org/search/空く
